observations:
LM2 Torah 30 is structurally too sparse to yield independent packages from bechina connections at this time.

The source text contains two bechina-style equations expressed through acronym/letter-reading rather than explicit 'בְּחִינַת' language:
1. בְּכִיָּה ↔ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם (weeping = Israel as sand of the sea) — acronym equation
2. מִסְפַּר ↔ מִסֵּפֶר (number = from the book) — gematria/reading equation

However, neither of these produces a network of 3+ concepts connected through bechina language that would form an independent thematic domain. The Torah is a 4-sentence teaching with a single conceptual move, and its architecture is primarily eitza (causal):
- דְּמָעוֹת הַחִדּוּשִׁים → סֵפֶר חָדָשׁ → protection against גְּזֵרוֹת הָאֻמּוֹת
- דְּמָעוֹת עֵשָׂו → power of nations (this good/evil mirror is structural, not a bechina cluster)

The good/evil mirror of tears (דְּמָעוֹת הַחִדּוּשִׁים vs. דְּמָעוֹת עֵשָׂו) is a compelling conceptual pair, but the Torah does not expand either cluster with additional bechina-linked concepts. Each 'side' of the mirror is represented by only 1–2 nodes, falling below the threshold of 3+ concepts needed to propose a new package.

Recommendation: Enter the following bechina edges into the dataset once confirmed:
- בְּכִיָּה ↔ חוֹל הַיָּם (reference 1030, type 'bechina') — weeping shares the essential nature of sand: boundary-protection against an overwhelming force
- דְּמָעוֹת הַחִדּוּשִׁים ↔ דְּמָעוֹת עֵשָׂו (reference 1030, type 'bechina', is_bad for the evil node) — these are two expressions of the same form (tears) at opposite polarities; their shared nature is precisely why one cancels the other
If these edges are entered and additional bechina connections are discovered from cross-referencing other Torahs, revisit package formation for this Torah.
